input.brief: Zonehunt outdoor pursuit game with play zone, chaser map and runner compass

style.name: Accent ladder
style.basis: 3 screens: a newsletter home, a network analytics overview, a cap-table company home
style.idea: One brand hue at full strength only on small marks, and its pale tints doing all the area work: the active nav row, a plan card, badges and progress tracks.
style.colourBudget: 3-10%, nearly all of it as pale tints of the one hue
style.signature: The full hue goes only on small marks: the one filled-button style, the data series and the active nav icon. Its 50-200 tints carry every area: the active nav row (tint fill with the dark ink of the hue), the plan or trial card, badges and progress tracks. The primary action may instead be near-black, as on the study's newsletter home.
identity: The ladder built from the brand's own hue (its logo, the brief's object) in place of the dealt raspberry: the full hue on small marks, its pale tints on areas, never violet or indigo.
The product's objects in the lead block: the newsletter's latest issue as its cover, the shop's products as 40px thumbnails, the course's lessons with their own art.
A ground one level toward the hue's palest tint (#fbf7f8 for the raspberry) in place of #f9fafb, so the page and the tints read as one family.
avoid: the full hue on large areas
a second accent family (four families on one screen was flagged in the study)
a gradient on the trial chip or upgrade button
a left accent bar on the active nav row on top of the tint (seen once in 23 screens)
style.notes: All three studied screens of this kind used violet, purple or pink as the one hue. The move does not depend on the hue, so the house's violet and indigo ban holds and the library deals a raspberry instead.

shell.name: Open plane

numbers.sidebarWidth: 230-256 (230, 240, 256 in the study; 280 and 292 with a built-in icon rail)
numbers.separation: none, or one 1px hairline; the sidebar sits on the page ground or within 1-2% of it
numbers.activeItem: neutral grey pill, radius 6-12, inset 8-12px from the sidebar edges (#e9e9e9-#ededed)
numbers.canvas: fluid with a 24-64px gutter, or a centred 1100px column

shell.blueprint: The labelled sidebar sits on the page ground with nothing or one hairline between it and the canvas; there is no top bar, and the page header and cards sit straight on the ground about 32-36px from the top. Workspace or account switcher at the top of the sidebar, primary nav on a 34px pitch, groups under 12-13px sentence-case grey labels with 22-56px of air above, utilities and the user row pushed to the bottom. Cards are white on the off-white ground (or the sidebar is white with a 1px border on a #f9fafb canvas). The canvas is fluid with one gutter value, or a centred column for personal homes.
shell.phone: The sidebar folds into a 48px top bar holding the screen's name, a menu button that opens a full-screen sheet with the nav and the switcher, and at most one action. Content takes the full width with 16px margins.

pattern.name: KPI strip, main chart and a side rail
pattern.basis: a newsletter home; a community overview
pattern.blueprint: Title row: a 24px noun or the product's name at 600-700, an optional 14-16px grey line under it, and the one primary action on the right, bottom-aligned with that line. 16-24px below, the scope row: section tabs and the date range in one row of 32-36px controls, or a 48px segmented track with the range select inside its right end. Then a grid of 1fr and a fixed 384px rail with a 24px gap. Main column: one KPI container split by 1px dividers into 3-5 equal cells (14px grey label, 24px value at 400-600, a 12px caption naming the baseline and window), then the main chart card, which is the largest thing on the screen, then the next card, all 16px apart. Rail: 16px headings outside their cards, 8px above each and 16px after the previous card; a recent-items list of 3-5 rows on a 45px pitch with 1px rules, closed by a 30px outlined 'View all' button instead of pagination. The rail starts level with the first card, not with the title.
pattern.phone: The rail moves below the main column; the KPI container becomes a 2-column grid; tabs scroll inside their own row.

pattern.name: Count cards that filter
pattern.blueprint: Above a list, 3-5 equal count cards (61px tall, 12px padding, a 13px grey label over a 16/600 value, 8px gap) are the type filter: the selected card gets a 1.5px accent border and a pale accent fill, and the list below shows that type only. Zero counts print as '0' in the same style; no deltas, no icons. This is one place where a row of identical small cards is right: the cards are peers and each one does work.
pattern.phone: The count cards become a horizontally scrolling row of chips with the count inside each, or a select above the list.

pattern.name: Object header and a six-column grid
pattern.blueprint: The page header is the object itself: one card (88px, 14px padding) holding a 50x62 cover, the 18/600 name with 28px icon buttons beside it (open, copy, share), a 13px grey meta line (date, time, place) and outlined 36px actions on the right. Under it, underline tabs on a full-width 1px rule, then a 36px row with a segmented time range on the left and a refresh button on the right. The body is one 6-column grid with one gutter (14px) in both directions whose spans change by row while every edge lands on the same lines: 3 KPI tiles of 2 columns, the main chart in 4 columns beside a side chart in 2, two progress cards of 3, a full-width trend of 6. Give the widest card to the screen's question, and do not give 824px to one ring and one legend row (flagged).
pattern.phone: The header card keeps cover, name and meta, with actions in a kebab; every grid item takes the full width in the same order.
